model: Look-through owner-FCF DCF on IGO's 24.99% economic share of Greenbushes, net of Kwinana and corporate drags (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY0 = FY2026 look-through revenue: 24.99% (49% of TLEA x 51% of Talison) x Greenbushes 100%-basis revenue A$2,858M (FY26 AR p.32). NOT IGO's consolidated A$462.9M, which is Nova nickel revenue that ceases by Dec-2026. Kwinana revenue (A$159M, 100%) is excluded from the revenue base and handled as a drag on the margin path.
inputs.share_count_basis: 757.27M ordinary shares on issue (FY26 AR) + 3.85M performance rights + 1.70M service rights outstanding at 30 June 2026 (share-based payment notes, lines 9617/9812) = 762.8M fully diluted; held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows. No buybacks in the history; no non-SBC issuance expected.
inputs.net_debt_note: IGO parent level only: cash A$386.5M less A$16.8M interest-bearing liabilities (all lease liabilities; bank facility undrawn) at 30 June 2026. The Lithium Business's own debt (Windfield's US$1.35B drawn loan) is deducted separately in equity_bridge on a look-through basis. Listed equity securities (A$99.1M) are in equity_bridge, not cash.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 AR segment note: share-based payments expense A$9.3M (line 7495); no equity-award tax withholding disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 in kpis)
inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner FCF FY26 = reported FCF 129.3 - SBC 9.3 - interest income 13.3 = 106.7. This is IGO's CONSOLIDATED (Nova-era) owner FCF, recorded for auditability only; it is not the projection base. Projections compound from base_revenue (look-through Greenbushes) via the driver paths. Note TLEA paid IGO no dividends in FY26 (AR p.30), so consolidated FCF carries none of the Lithium Business's A$2.1B EBITDA.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD flows, AUD-built rate: Australian 10y bond ~4.3% + ERP 5.5% x beta ~1.15 = ~10.6% cost of equity; Talison's Windfield loan is deducted in the bridge rather than blended into a WACC, so the 10.5% rate is effectively a cost of equity for an unlevered look-through stake. Risk is charged ONCE: lithium-price cyclicality and the Kwinana outcome live in the scenario flows; the ~1pp above a 9.5% AUD large-cap miner baseline prices the structural non-control/cash-trapping risk of a 24.99% minority stake whose cash must pass Windfield -> TLEA -> IGO with Tianqi's consent (zero dividends received in FY26 despite Greenbushes EBITDA of A$2.1B). Same WACC in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) leases as debt: IGO's A$16.8M lease liabilities sit in total_debt; lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows. Immaterial either way at the parent level.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the revenue base: the 24.99% look-through (49% of TLEA x 51% of Talison) makes every Greenbushes flow attributable-only, so no NCI deduction appears in the bridge. Kwinana is 100% TLEA-owned, so IGO bears 49% of its losses; that 49% share is what the Kwinana drag in the margin path represents.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: owner-FCF DCF is wrong on IGO's consolidated statements because the consolidated revenue (Nova nickel, A$449M) is being divested by Dec-2026 (A$7M sale to Global Lithium Resources, ACCC waiver 2026-09-23) and the real earnings engine (Greenbushes) is equity-accounted as one P&L line. The routing table has no JV-holdco row, so this is a sum-of-parts run through the engine: (1) the operating part is a look-through owner-FCF DCF on IGO's 24.99% share of Greenbushes, an operating mine with its own revenue, EBITDA (73.4% FY26), capex (A$356M FY26, A$250-300M FY27 guide) and 30% tax, discounted at an AUD cost of equity; (2) the drags on that stream that IGO cannot avoid (49% of Kwinana's cash burn; IGO corporate, exploration and Cosmos care-and-maintenance costs; SBC) are built into the margin paths as a percent of look-through revenue; (3) the parent balance sheet, listed securities, look-through Windfield net debt, Nova's residual months and the retained Cosmos rehabilitation liability are in equity_bridge. FY26 calibration: look-through EBITDA 57% x 714 = ~A$407M less D&A/tax/capex gives ~A$200M owner FCF, against IGO's A$207.3M equity-accounted TLEA profit share (which is after Talison's ~A$140M interest, 24.99% of which is ~A$35M, and before IGO's ~A$85M corporate/exploration) - the two tie within the non-operating noise. MID-CYCLE PRICING: FY26 realised ~US$1,320/t SC6 average (Q4 US$2,286/t; spot ~US$2,000/t mid-2026); base fades to ~US$1,450/t by FY29, bull holds ~US$1,700/t, bear reverts to ~US$1,150/t. SBC is small but non-zero (A$9.3M, ~1.3% of look-through revenue) so house and street bands are distinct but narrow. All money in millions of AUD.

equity_bridge.item: Listed equity securities at fair value (matching asset for the A$33M FV gain excluded from the flows)
equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR segment note line 7507 / note 9097; A$63.8M FY25

equity_bridge.item: Look-through share of Windfield/TLEA net debt
equity_bridge.note: Windfield corporate loan US$1,350M drawn = A$1,965.4M (FY26 AR note 23); TLEA consolidated financial liabilities A$2,173.7M less cash A$423.9M = A$1,749.8M net. IGO look-through: 24.99% of the Windfield loan (A$491M) plus 24.99% of the A$208M of other financial liabilities/leases (A$52M), less 24.99% of TLEA cash assumed to sit in Talison (A$106M) = ~A$437M, rounded to A$440M. Interest on this debt is NOT charged in the flows (EV framework), so deducting the debt here charges it once.

equity_bridge.item: Nova residual net cash to closure (mining to ~Dec-2026, stockpiles, WC unwind, less closure/redundancy cash)
equity_bridge.note: FY26 Nova EBITDA A$158M; 4Q26 A$31M after A$31M of year-end provisions (underlying ~A$62M/qtr). Two more quarters at declining grades ~A$100M EBITDA, less ~A$30M closure/redundancy cash already provided, negligible capex, positive WC release; rehabilitation transfers to Global Lithium Resources on completion. A$7M sale consideration ignored.

equity_bridge.item: Retained Cosmos rehabilitation provision (Nova's share transfers with the sale)
equity_bridge.note: Total provision A$115.5M at 30 June 2026 (note 12); no segment split disclosed. Forrestania's transferred provision was A$69.4M; assume ~A$60M is Nova's and ~A$55M is Cosmos's, which stays with IGO. Cosmos ongoing care-and-maintenance cost (~A$10-12M/yr) is inside the corporate drag in the margin path.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 5-year look-through revenue CAGR FY26-FY31 (volume ramp to ~1.9Mt on CGP3 plus partial price recovery to mid-cycle); historical CAGRs are not usable as a forward anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All historical CAGRs describe the consolidated Nova/Forrestania nickel business being wound down and the FY23 lithium-price peak (FY23 owner FCF A$1,058M, FY26 A$107M). Equity CAGR is dominated by the FY25 A$1.2B TLEA/Kwinana impairment. None of them describes the go-forward business, which is a 24.99% stake in Greenbushes.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series used for the FCF CAGRs: FY21 344.0 (351.3-4.9-2.4), FY23 1,057.8 (1,077.9-11.8-8.3), FY26 106.7 (129.3-9.3-13.3). Owner-FCF CAGRs are only modestly below reported-FCF CAGRs; SBC is not growing faster than cash flow here - the collapse is price and divestment, not stock comp.

base.growth_note: FY27: production guide 1,550-1,750kt (mid 1,650kt, +17% on 1,410kt) x price ~US$1,450/t average (A$2,230, up ~10% on FY26's ~US$1,320 average, well below the US$2,286 Q4 realisation) = ~A$3.7B 100%-basis. FY28-29: volume to ~1.9Mt as CGP3 reaches nameplate, price fading to mid-cycle ~US$1,450/t. Thereafter 2.5% nominal (flat real price, flat volume).
base.ebitda_margin_note: Greenbushes mine margin ~73-75% at A$2,200/t (cash cost A$415/t + 5% WA royalty + ~A$30/t offsite G&A), LESS the 49% Kwinana share (A$75M FY27 falling to A$15M by FY31 as Train 1 is fixed or mothballed: ~7% -> 1.5% of look-through revenue), LESS IGO corporate ~A$40M post-Nova + exploration A$35-40M (guided) + Cosmos C&M ~A$10M = ~A$85M (~8% of revenue, slowly diluting). FY26 calibration at 57% ties to the equity-accounted TLEA profit share (see inputs.notes).
base.da_note: Talison's D&A is currently small relative to capex (legacy assets largely depreciated; CGP3 only commissioned FY26): backed out from TLEA's A$570.5M tax expense at 30% implies Talison pre-tax ~A$1.9B on A$2.1B EBITDA less ~A$140M interest. D&A rises toward capex as CGP3 and deferred stripping depreciate. Only affects the tax shield.
base.capex_note: FY27 guide A$250-300M (100%) on ~A$3.7B revenue = ~7%; steady-state sustaining + deferred waste ~A$250M on ~A$4.2B = 6%. Kwinana's capex is inside the Kwinana drag in the margin path (FY26's A$167M EBITDA loss already included A$84M of capitalised expenditure expensed by IGO).
base.tax_note: Talison pays 30% Australian corporate tax; dividends up the chain are franked. IGO's own corporate/exploration costs are netted in EBIT before tax, which slightly overstates their deductibility - conservative direction ignored.

bull.growth_note: Lithium deficit thesis holds: FY27 realised ~US$1,750/t (A$2,700) on 1,700kt; volume to ~1.95Mt by FY29 at ~US$1,700/t sustained; 3% nominal thereafter.
bull.ebitda_margin_note: Higher price lifts the mine margin toward 78-80% (Q4 FY26 printed 80%); Kwinana resolved by FY29 (drag to zero); corporate/exploration held flat in dollars so the % drag shrinks.

bear.growth_note: Price reverts to the FY25 trough band ~US$1,150/t (A$1,770) as Chinese/African supply responds; volume ramp (1,650kt -> 1,850kt) only just offsets it. 2% nominal thereafter.
bear.ebitda_margin_note: Mine margin ~69% at A$1,770/t, LESS a Kwinana burn that is never resolved (49% x ~A$150M = ~A$75M/yr, ~9% of look-through revenue), LESS corporate/exploration/Cosmos ~A$85M (~10%).

scenario_narratives.base: Post-Nova IGO is a 24.99% look-through stake in Greenbushes. CGP3 takes production from 1.41Mt to ~1.9Mt by FY29 while the realised spodumene price settles at a mid-cycle ~US$1,450/t - below the Q4 FY26 print of US$2,286 and mid-2026 spot of ~US$2,000, above the FY25-26 trough. The mine margin stays ~73-75% (A$415/t cash cost against a ~A$2,200/t price). Kwinana Train 1 is either fixed or mothballed over FY27-FY31, so IGO's 49% share of its burn fades from ~A$75M to ~A$15M. Corporate, exploration and Cosmos care-and-maintenance run ~A$85M/yr with no new project reaching production inside the horizon. Dividends resume up the Windfield-TLEA-IGO chain but at Tianqi's cadence, which the 10.5% AUD rate prices.
scenario_narratives.bull: The lithium market moves into deficit in late 2026 as delayed greenfield supply meets storage-led demand; Greenbushes realises ~US$1,700/t through FY29 and prints Q4-FY26-style 78-80% margins on ~1.95Mt. Tianqi and IGO resolve Kwinana by FY29 (restructure or exit) and the drag goes to zero. Greenbushes' Strategic Options Review (steeper pit, lower strip, underground resource) supports 3% terminal growth and a 14x cap. The A$99M listed securities and net cash fund BioHeap copper without dilution.
scenario_narratives.bear: Spodumene reverts to ~US$1,150/t as Chinese lepidolite and African supply restarts on the 2026 price rally, and the volume ramp merely offsets price. Kwinana is never resolved: Train 1 keeps missing guidance, IGO keeps absorbing ~A$75M/yr of losses, and Tianqi keeps cash inside TLEA (as in FY26, when no dividends were paid). Corporate and exploration spend continues without a producing successor to Nova. Terminal multiple 10x. The bear does not hit the zero floor - Greenbushes is cash-positive even here - but there is no cash return to IGO shareholders for years.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: after Nova, IGO's value rests on a single non-controlled asset, Kwinana's future is explicitly 'not yet resolved' (FY26 AR), TLEA paid no dividends in FY26, and the CFO seat has turned over twice in a year. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs two independent things - a sustained lithium price above US$1,700/t AND a Kwinana resolution with Tianqi - and the FY26 CGP3 fire showed operational risk at the one asset that matters. Base 45%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value IGO as what it is about to become: a minority, non-operating look-through interest in the world's best hard-rock lithium mine, priced at mid-cycle rather than spot, with the losses IGO cannot avoid (Kwinana, corporate, exploration, Cosmos) charged against the stream and the Talison debt deducted once in the bridge. The consolidated statements (Nova) are ignored as a projection base because that business ends in December 2026; Nova's remaining months are a bridge item. The stake's structural cash-trapping risk is charged once, in a 10.5% AUD discount rate, and cyclicality is charged once, in the scenario flows. Historical CAGRs are reported but explicitly not used.
key_risks_to_valuation: Spodumene price: at ~74% mine margin, value moves close to one-for-one with price; the base uses US$1,450/t mid-cycle against US$2,000+ spot, so the market is currently paying for something nearer spot
Kwinana resolution: the difference between the base (drag fades) and bear (drag persists) is ~A$60M/yr of look-through FCF, worth ~A$0.60/share
Cash trapped in TLEA/Windfield: no FY26 dividend despite A$2.1B Greenbushes EBITDA; Windfield's US$1.35B loan (expiring May 2029) takes priority over distributions
Look-through net debt estimate (A$440M) relies on assumptions about where TLEA's A$424M cash sits; a A$100M error is ~A$0.13/share
Corporate/exploration spend (~A$85M/yr) with no committed successor project; the bull's BioHeap copper optionality is not in any scenario's flows
Greenbushes operational risk concentrated in one site (June 2026 CGP3 fire cost ~7 weeks of ramp-up)
